newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees bright 1997 investment prospects.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees bright 1997 investment prospects.

text.p: Indonesia has good investment prospects in 1997 with its economy expected to expand steadily despite an investment slowdown this year, Investment Minister Sanyoto Sastrowardoyo said on Friday.
Sanyoto told a year-end news briefing the government would continue to abolish unnecessary levies and simplify investment procedures.
He said foreign investment approvals dropped to $29.9 billion this year from $39.9 billion in 1995.
"The value in foreign investment approval is lower, but the number of projects rose to 959 from 799 in 1995. I am optimistic for next year," Sanyoto said.
"We cannot say how much investment there will be next year. We only can say the prospect for next year is bright. We hope the figure and the projects will be higher," he said.
The minister said the government was committed to maintaining and improving the investment climate through rational macro-economic policies to achieve high growth.
"We have experienced a steady high economic growth rate and we can contain inflation, so we are still attractive for foreign investors," Sanyoto said.
"We will continue to deregulate our economy and to keep the investment climate attractive and competitive...," he added.

He said Japan topped the list of foreign investment approvals with $7.7 billion in 1996, compared with $3.8 billion in 1995. British investment approvals dropped to $3.4 billion in 1996 from $6.3 billion in 1995.
Sanyoto said chemical industries, steel, pulp, textiles and food were the major projects in 1996.
He added that foreign investment realisation was 55 percent in 1995 compared with 51 percent in 1994.
The Industry and Trade Ministry said on Thursday that the government expected economic growth of between 7.6 and 8.0 percent in 1997, with inflation below 7.0 percent.
The economy was expected to expand by 7.6 to 7.9 percent this year, with inflation seen between 6.5 and 6.8 percent.
